source.title: Towards scientific discovery with dictionary learning: Extracting biological concepts from microscopy foundation models
source.authors: Konstantin Donhauser; Kristina Ulicna; Gemma E. Moran; Aditya Ravuri; Kian Kenyon-Dean; Cian Eastwood; Jason S. Hartford

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies dictionary learning and reports reconstruction quality and label-probe results for SAE reconstructions, but it does not investigate whether the unreconstructed error is structured, predictable, or functionally causal as the claim versions specify.
record.gate_note: The paper compares ICFL and TopK SAE reconstruction quality and the biological label information retained by their reconstructions. These results are recorded as related findings, not as tests of a listed version. Dead-feature counts and other values used to motivate methods are not results about the claimed structure or function of SAE error.
record.test_reason: The study applies ICFL and TopK SAEs to a microscopy MAE (MAE-G). It reports reconstruction cosine similarity, dead-feature counts, selectivity and linear-probe accuracy on reconstructions. It never analyses the reconstruction error itself: no linear prediction of the error, no per-token error norms across SAE sizes, no spliced-in loss against random errors, and no circuit or steering analysis with or without the error term. The ICFL-vs-TopK cosine gap shows that the size of the error depends on the algorithm. It does not show whether dark matter is a training artifact, so it belongs under fits_no_version. The conclusion only speculates that incomplete features may reflect DL technique, model scale, or nonlinear representation. That is discussion, not a test.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors find that ICFL with control-based PCA whitening extracts biologically meaningful features, and that ICFL and whitening improve selectivity over TopK SAEs. They also say the sparse features are clearly incomplete, with probe accuracy dropping on subtle morphology tasks. They leave open whether this comes from DL technique, model scale, or nonlinear representation.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops ICFL with PCA whitening and compares it with TopK SAEs for biological feature extraction; it does not implement or evaluate the claimed dark-matter analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: Reconstruction and probing outcomes vary with the dictionary-learning method, PCA whitening, and sparsity; the text says whitening has a stronger effect on probing accuracy than increasing sparsity.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear probes on ICFL and TopK reconstructions keep nearly all signal for cell type, batch and strong CRISPR tasks. They lose signal significantly on the siRNA and functional-group tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse reconstructions of vision-MAE activations lose task-relevant linear information, most on subtle distinctions.

fits_no_version.finding: ICFL (matching-pursuit encoder) reconstructs with higher cosine similarity than TopK SAE at every tested sparsity. It also has far fewer dead features (55 vs 7640 without whitening; 341 vs 8026 with).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The size of the reconstruction error depends on the encoding and training algorithm at fixed sparsity.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning; Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267 (2025)
record.problems: The relevant reconstruction and probing outcomes are shown in figures without exact values in the text. The study does not test residual structure, error norms across SAE sizes, random-error comparisons, or effects on model loss, circuits, or steering.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were omitted. Exact plotted values are not transcribed because the text does not state them.

untested.parts: Linear predictability of the SAE error from the input activation.
Per-token error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, shared failure contexts, and persistence of the error with scale.
Loss effect of splicing in reconstructions compared with same-norm random errors.
Split of the error into a linear part holding unlearned features and a nonlinear part that resists further dictionary learning.
Loss of circuit or steering behaviour when the error term is dropped.
Whether dark matter is a training artifact. Only total reconstruction fidelity across two algorithms is shown, with no decomposition of the error.

record.verdict_notes: There is no relation value for 'neither uses nor cites'. 'discusses' is kept only because the conclusion speculates on why sparse features are incomplete. The paper does not cite the original dark-matter paper. All quantitative reconstruction results are figure-only.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of SAE error is linearly predictable from the input activation.
Per-token error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, overlap in contexts where larger and smaller SAEs fail, and error persistence with scale.
Whether SAE reconstruction errors harm model loss more than same-size random errors.
Whether linear error contains unlearned features and nonlinear error resists further dictionary learning.
Whether SAE-feature-based circuits or steering lose model behavior unless the error term is retained.
Whether dark matter is mainly a training artifact and shrinks with improved architectures or end-to-end training.

rows.subject: MAE-G
rows.stage_stated: masked autoencoder trained on cellular microscopy images
rows.operation_detail: Compared linear-probe accuracy on the original representation and ICFL reconstruction for simple classification tasks.

conditions.value: cell type (1), batch (2), and strong CRISPR perturbation (4)

rows.measure: Balanced test accuracy for biological-label classification from reconstructed representations.
rows.baseline: Original representation x; exact values not stated in text.
rows.value: Almost the entire signal is preserved; exact values are figure only.
rows.note: The authors describe near-complete preservation for these simpler tasks. This is label information in activations, not a measure of model behavior or error structure.
rows.check: This measures biological-label probe accuracy on reconstructions, not model behaviour or loss. The state cannot be read against any version.

rows.subject: MAE-G
rows.stage_stated: masked autoencoder trained on cellular microscopy images
rows.operation_detail: Compared linear-probe accuracy on the original representation and ICFL reconstruction for difficult classification tasks.

conditions.value: siRNA perturbations (3) and functional gene groups (5)

rows.measure: Balanced test accuracy for biological-label classification from reconstructed representations.
rows.baseline: Original representation x; exact values not stated in text.
rows.value: A substantial amount of the linear signal is preserved, with a significant drop for subtle morphology tasks; exact values are figure only.
rows.note: The authors call the sparse features incomplete on tasks involving subtle morphological changes.
rows.check: Same as r1. The probe drop on hard tasks is label information lost from the reconstruction, not a measure of model function carried by the error.

rows.baseline: TopK SAE at the same sparsity; exact values not stated in text.
rows.value: Higher reconstruction quality than TopK SAE at the same sparsity; exact values are figure only.
rows.note: Text says the ICFL advantage persists across sparsity levels. This compares reconstruction methods; it does not measure error predictability or error norms.
rows.check: This row compares the study's own method (ICFL) against TopK. It shows relative reconstruction fidelity, not dark-matter structure. Keep it as a related finding only. The value is figure-only (Fig 4C, Fig 9).
